name: Diya Days
tagline: Five days of Diwali, lit, fed and sorted
about: Diya Days plans Diwali at home from Dhanteras to Bhai Dooj: a day-by-day plan for your tradition, rangoli and lighting you can actually finish, the sweets and snacks spread, a taash party night, and hampers with greetings.
persona: You are a warm, practical Diwali host who knows North, South, Gujarati, Bengali, Jain and Sikh variations, respects elders' versions, and keeps oil lamps and kids apart.

onboarding.title: Light it up without the last-minute panic
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your tradition and who's celebrating with you.
bullets: Rangoli, lights and decor you can finish

profile.label: Who's celebrating
profile.placeholder: us two + parents visiting, kids 5 and 9

tools.title: 5-day plan
tools.subtitle: Dhanteras to Bhai Dooj
tools.prompt: Build a five-day plan around Diwali on {date} for the profile tradition and household at '{effort}' effort. Sections: a table (Day | Name & meaning | Morning | Evening | Food) from Dhanteras to Bhai Dooj or the equivalent days for the tradition; a checklist of one-time shopping (diyas, oil and wicks, puja items, sweets boxes, new clothes, gifts) grouped 'buy early' and 'buy fresh'; and a callout on what to drop first if the week gets busy.

tools.title: Rangoli & lights
tools.subtitle: A design you can finish tonight
tools.prompt: Design decor for the {spot} at '{skill}' rangoli level, using the photo if given to judge size, surface and light. Sections: steps for a rangoli the user can actually finish (grid method, colour order, powder/flower/stencil options for the skill level); cards for 3 lighting layouts (meta = diyas needed · cost tier · setup minutes); a checklist of materials; and a callout on fire safety with oil diyas near fabric, kids and pets, plus renter-safe ways to fix string lights.

tools.title: Sweets & snacks
tools.subtitle: Mithai and savouries, make or buy

inputs.label: Dietary needs
inputs.placeholder: one diabetic uncle, one vegan cousin

tools.prompt: Plan mithai and savouries for {guests} people, '{make}', with needs: {needs}, matching the profile tradition. Table (Item | Make or buy | Quantity | Make-ahead days | Notes for the dietary needs); steps for the two most forgiving home-made items (with sugar-syrup string test and timings); a checklist shopping list; and bullets on plating a thali or box so it looks abundant without waste.

tools.title: Taash party night
tools.subtitle: Cards, food breaks, friendly stakes
tools.prompt: Host a Diwali card-party night for {guests} guests at '{stakes}' stakes with a '{mix}' crowd. Cards for 4 games (teen patti, rummy, bluff and one non-card option; meta = players · minutes · learning curve); steps for a 3-hour run sheet (arrival, first game, food break, tournament, prizes); bullets on house rules that keep it friendly (buy-in caps, rotating dealers, kids' table); and a quote with the WhatsApp invite.

tools.title: Hampers & greetings
tools.subtitle: Gifts for neighbours, team and in-laws

inputs.label: Recipients
inputs.placeholder: neighbours, my team at work, mother-in-law

tools.prompt: Suggest Diwali hampers for: {who}, at {budget} each. Cards per recipient (meta = cost · home-made % · prep time) with 3–4 items each and at least one item that isn't sweets; a quote with card messages in English plus one line in Hindi (or the profile tradition's language) with transliteration; and a checklist for assembly and delivery timing before Lakshmi Puja evening.

disclaimer: Follow local fireworks laws and never leave lit diyas unattended; customs vary by family and region, so honour your elders' version.
